# Onboard a new employee

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

After a hire is accepted and before the employee takes on their role and access. A completed role-specific onboarding plan with verified access, required training and an owned initial review.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Confirm the role, start conditions and private records

agent-runnable


Gather the accepted employment terms, manager, work location and approved start date. HR checks unresolved right-to-work, payroll or local prerequisites using the hiring process without copying sensitive identity records into a public checklist.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Prepare a role-specific onboarding schedule

agent-runnable


Plan introductions, first assignments, equipment, payroll and benefits handoffs, policy orientation and support contacts. Assign owners and clarify which tasks depend on the employee or an external provider.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Provision approved equipment and least-privilege access

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized administrators use the workspace-user and device-management processes to grant only the approved role. Verify the employee can access required systems and that account recovery and asset ownership belong to the company.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Complete orientation and supervised first work

human · human approval required


The manager introduces the team, expectations, safety and security reporting routes and role-specific practices. The employee completes their own required training and acknowledges policies through the applicable process.

- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review readiness and close onboarding gaps

human · human approval required


Check the employee can perform an agreed initial task and knows how to get help. Record outstanding access or training, assign owners and schedule a manager review of objectives and support needs.

- Verify: A completed role-specific onboarding plan with verified access, required training and an owned initial review.
- Sources: [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
